questions.q: What does split conformal prediction use to set the interval width?
options: Absolute residuals on a separate calibration set
The standard deviation of the series
why: Training residuals are too small because the model has seen those points.
Correct: residuals on data the model did not train on.
The series spread is not the forecast error.

questions.q: n = 49 calibration residuals, α = 0.2. Which rank k do you take?
Sorted residuals: 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 (n = 9). α = 0.2, so k = 8. The forecast is 100. What is the interval?
why: Correct: the 8th smallest residual is 6, so the interval is 100 ± 6.
That uses the largest residual 9. It would be for k = 9.
That uses residual 4, which is the 6th smallest.

questions.q: Why can a static conformal interval under-cover in a time series?
options: The error level can change after the calibration period
why: More residuals would make the estimate more stable.
Correct: trend, drift or higher noise make new errors larger than the calibration errors.
Conformal does not need normal errors.

questions.q: A rolling window of the last 30 residuals is used. What is the main trade-off in choosing a smaller window?
options: It adapts faster but the quantile estimate is noisier
It is slower and more exact
It removes the need for calibration
why: Correct: few residuals react quickly but give a noisy quantile (and k may exceed n).
A smaller window uses fewer values and is not more exact.
You still need residuals from data the model did not train on.

questions.q: You make a 7-step-ahead forecast for day t. Which 7-step residuals can the rolling window use?
options: Those of target days up to t - 7
Those of target days up to t
Those of target days up to t + 7
why: Correct: the 7-step forecast for target day d is made at day d - 7, and the actual of day d arrives on day d. When you forecast day t, only residuals of target days up to t - 7 are known.
The actual of day t is not known when you forecast it.
These actuals are in the future.

questions.q: In ACI with γ = 0.01 and α = 0.1, the interval missed (err = 1) and α_t = 0.1. What is α_{t+1}?
questions.why: α_{t+1} = 0.1 + 0.01 × (0.1 − 1) = 0.1 − 0.009 = 0.091. A smaller α means a wider interval.
